title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with activity as the Space Force reorganizes its procurement strategies and awards significant contracts, while private players like Sierra Space and True Anomaly secure critical funding. Amidst these developments, the specter of hypersonic testing delays looms large, reminding us that ambition often comes with its share of turbulence.

themes.title: Space Force's Procurement Overhaul
themes.body: The Space Force has completed a significant reorganization, creating nine distinct acquisition portfolios aimed at streamlining procurement processes. This move is likely to enhance agility in responding to emerging threats and technologies, though it may also invite scrutiny over its execution.

themes.title: Funding Flows in Private Sector
themes.body: True Anomaly's recent $190 million Series C funding round underscores the growing investor appetite for space startups, particularly those focused on defense applications. Meanwhile, Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant has cleared a critical design review, positioning it as a strong contender in upcoming government contracts.

themes.title: Hypersonic Testing Woes
themes.body: The third consecutive delay in hypersonic glide-vehicle testing raises questions about the reliability of current technologies and the pace of innovation. As competitors ramp up their efforts, the U.S. risks falling behind in a critical area of defense.

themes.title: New Markets and Partnerships
themes.body: Anduril and L3Harris's collaboration on a tactical SDA constellation bid reflects a trend toward strategic partnerships in the space domain. Additionally, the exploration of new markets, as highlighted by Golden Dome, indicates a shift towards diversifying revenue streams amid increasing competition.
